subject: MSstatsPTM: same modification site, but distinct PTM

messages.author: d3cb5abb144524de
messages.subject: MSstatsPTM: same modification site, but distinct PTM
parts:
Hi MSstats team,

For the carbonylation PTMs I have been able to identify I have found some "hotspots" where the same Lys is being modified by different adducts (up to 6 distinct PTMs per site).

As these adducts might not be related I am inclined to test for significant difference individually. To consider this at the moment I am adapting the MSstatsPTM input as:

Protein_ModSite_MassShift

I want to double check if this is a reasonable analysis with MSstatsPTM or you would suggest something different.

In advance, thank you for your time.
Sincerely,
Juan C.

messages.author: 13904eb0f06097b0
messages.subject: Re: MSstatsPTM: same modification site, but distinct PTM
parts:
Hi Juan,

Apologies, I remember this question. I think Google might have autodeleted my comment (we were having major problems with that last year).

Yes this seems like a perfectly reasonable way to use MSstatsPTM. In this case the package will summarize all features for each peptidoform separately and then use the summarized values to fit an individual model to each peptidoform. One note is that you may have very few features (peptide ions) for each peptidoform, so the analysis will be very sensitive to any messiness in the data (outliers/missing values/high variance/ect).

I hope this makes sense!

Best,
Devon
